title: AGT-12: prioritize interface-change review context
body:
## Scope
Implement only AGT-12 (PRD §3.8.7 / TS §8.7). Review investigation paths now prioritize changed sources and linked acceptance/boundary tests, including unchanged tests, ahead of unrelated changed tests. Stable deduplication and model exclusions apply before selection.

Full, recheck and stateless packets carry candidate-bound `interfaceContext` guidance: resolve direct importers and callers of changed non-private interfaces/symbols with native `usages`, or disclose text-search fallback, before unrelated adjacent reads. Focused and native rubrics follow the same priority. Resolution is native/cooperative and remains unknown until evidenced; packet tests do not prove observed host execution or complete static/runtime coverage. No import scanner, schema, verdict, permissions or context-ceiling changes.

## Evidence
Independent local spec review completed; both findings dispositioned before implementation. Four distinguishing behavior cases failed before runtime edits; all five [AGT-12] tests now pass. Local typecheck, all lints, M0 coverage, build (783 KB under unchanged 800 KB), complete payload verification and reproducible-build checks pass. Staged and outgoing-range privacy scans found no likely leaks; these scans are not proof of absence.

Exact head `db009d16d14d6a8799c957ba322db170b5a94c2a` passed [untrusted run 42408244433](https://github.com/vedprakash-m/tenet/actions/runs/42408244433): Ubuntu and macOS full `npm run ci` each passed 1,752 tests with zero failures; built scratch-repository UAT passed on Node 24 and 22.12.0 on both platforms; Windows portability passed. The AGT-12 built scenario proves unchanged linked acceptance-test priority ahead of an unrelated changed test and unknown-resolution metadata, not observed native caller execution.

The first hosted run passed full CI but exposed a UAT fixture attribution error. `db009d1` declares both intentionally changed files in the existing comma-separated `--touched` option; no kernel semantics or assertion was weakened. This green run supersedes the changelog's publication-time pending validation note. Windows kernel mutations are unsupported by design; native-host resolution remains unobserved.

## Review and release
One feature PR on a non-main branch. Owner merges; no auto-merge. Preserve the solo 72-hour review window for executable/effects changes, with that limitation disclosed in release notes. Local feature spec is archived; review records and plan remain ignored and unpublished.

A read-only preview predicts a CHANGELOG conflict with capacity #9. No immediate branch rewrite: after the owner merges the prerequisite and explicitly authorizes an update, preserve all feature entries and corrected capacity disclosure without rebasing or force-pushing, then validate the resulting exact head.
